subject: Request: temporary SLA relief & monthly credit cap — Nimbus Analytics
messages:
From: Sarah Patel <sarah@nimbusanalytics.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nimbusanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary SLA relief while we migrate batch workloads

Hi Irene,

Quick context: we’re preparing a major migration of a set of batch inference jobs to a new data pipeline (windowed processing) that will run the week of May 3. During the migration we expect higher-than-normal error rates and occasional cold-starts while we warm caches and reconfigure prefixes. Our security/compliance team has asked that we align on a short-term SLA exception that acknowledges a slightly lower uptime floor for that migration window, and a pragmatic cap on monthly service credits so our procurement folks can sign the SOW.

Concretely, can Redwood consider: 1) a temporary lowering of the uptime floor from 99.9% to 99.5% for a 3-week window (May 3–May 23), and 2) a cap on monthly remedies/credits tied to either a fixed dollar amount or a percentage of committed spend? We’re asking because our legal team wants predictability on potential credits while we finalize the orchestration changes.

We’re trying to avoid delaying the migration — if we can get a short amendment, procurement can complete the PO. Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Thanks,
Sarah Patel
Head of Platform Engineering
Nimbus Analytics

[attachment: Service_Impact_Report_Mar-Apr.csv]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah@nimbusanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA relief while we migrate batch workloads

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear write-up and the impact report. Appreciate the heads-up on timing.

Short answer: we can accommodate a temporary exception but need to align internally on the guardrails (duration, remedy cap, and telemetry requirements). I’ve attached a short draft amendment that frames the exception and includes a proposed cap on total monthly remedies for the period. High-level proposal:

- Exception window: May 3, 2027 00:00 UTC — May 23, 2027 23:59 UTC
- Uptime floor during window: 99.5% (instead of standard 99.9%)
- Remedy cap: lesser of $8,000 USD or 4% of the monthly committed spend for Nimbus (for any single month overlapping exception window)
- Telemetry: Redwood will rely on standard availability telemetry; we’ll share an interim monthly report covering incidents and token-level impact for that period.

I’ll loop in product and legal for confirmation and will follow up within 48 hours with an agreed amendment or alternative. If that framing looks acceptable to procurement, we can draft the PO language to reflect the cap.

Next steps: I’m copying Ben (sales ops) and Marissa (legal) — Ben and Marissa, can you confirm we’re comfortable with the $8k / 4% cap and the three-week window? Laura — quick check on telemetry and whether we need any additional instrumentation for the migration so both sides have the same availability numbers.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198

[attachment: Draft_SLA_Amendment_v1.pdf]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: temporary SLA relief while we migrate batch workloads

Team — forwarding Nimbus’ request and my initial framing (see attached draft amendment). Key asks from Nimbus: 3-week exception window, uptime floor to 99.5%, and a remedy cap for the affected month. Procurement is pressing to have this spelled out so they can sign the SOW.

Specific questions:
- Legal/Finance: is $8k or 4% of committed spend (whichever is lower) an acceptable cap to offer as a one-off for onboarding risk?
- Product: will the standard availability telemetry be authoritative for the period, or do we need a short-term joint instrumentation step to avoid disputes?

I’d like to respond to Nimbus by EOD Thursday.

Thanks — Marissa/Ben/Laura, any redlines I should bake into the reply?

— Irene

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: temporary SLA relief while we migrate batch workloads

Irene — thanks for the heads-up. From a commercial and risk perspective I’d prefer a cap that scales with spend rather than a flat number. My recommendation: cap at the lesser of $12,000 USD or 5% of the monthly committed spend; this preserves predictability for the customer while covering our exposure. Also add a clause that the exception does not set precedent — language along the lines of ‘one-time, non-precedential amendment for migration window only.’

If Nimbus’ committed monthly spend is small (<$50k), the flat dollar cap helps them predict worst-case; if large, the percentage cap keeps our liability proportional.

Ben
Senior Sales Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: temporary SLA relief while we migrate batch workloads

Thanks — a couple product/ops notes:
- Standard availability telemetry should be sufficient if Nimbus runs canonical traffic through the production endpoints. If they will be routing to a staging-like pool, we’ll need explicit joint instrumentation (simple shared dashboard) to avoid measurement drift.
- Suggest tightening the window to 14 days (May 3–May 16) if Nimbus can phase migration in two waves; shorter window reduces our exposure and is easier to justify to finance.
- For remedies, instead of a single dollar cap, consider a two-tier cap: 1) for any single calendar month overlapping the window, cap remedies at the lesser of $10,000 or 5% of the monthly committed spend, and 2) overall cap across the full exception period equal to $15,000. That gives a blunt upper bound for both sides.

If legal and finance are okay, that’s the package I’d accept.

— Laura
VP, Product — Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah@nimbusanalytics.com>, procurement@nimbusanalytics.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 17:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA relief while we migrate batch workloads

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the clear ask and the impact report. After internal review we can agree to a short-term amendment that balances Nimbus’ need for predictability and Redwood’s exposure during onboarding. Below is the agreed language we can include in a one-page amendment to the MSA; we can convert this into PO/SOW language once you confirm.

Agreed amendment (summary):
- Exception window: May 3, 2027 00:00 UTC — May 16, 2027 23:59 UTC (14 calendar days)
- Uptime floor during window: 99.5% (temporary replacement of the standard 99.9% uptime commitment for the exception window only)
- Remedy cap: for any calendar month overlapping the exception window, remedies shall be capped at the lesser of $10,000 USD or 5% of the monthly committed spend; the aggregate remedies for the entire exception period shall not exceed $15,000 USD
- Measurement: Redwood’s standard availability telemetry will be used; if Nimbus routes traffic to non-production pools, both parties will provision a shared dashboard for the period to ensure measurement parity
- Non-precedential clause: this amendment is a one-time, non-precedential accommodation solely for the migration described in Nimbus’ Service_Impact_Report_Mar-Apr.csv

Next steps:
1) Please confirm that the 14-day window and the remedy caps above are acceptable to procurement.
2) If confirmed, we’ll send a short amendment PDF for signatures and concurrently update the SOW language for your PO team.
3) Laura will reach out to your platform lead to set up the shared dashboard if you plan to use a staging pool.

If you prefer a call, I’m available tomorrow morning (Fri) 9–11 PT.

Best regards,
Irene Choi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198
